newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Capita has cash to finance growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Capita has cash to finance growth.

text.p: British business outsourcing and support services firm Capita Group Plc reported a sharp jump in first-half profits on Tuesday and said it was well-positioned to finance organic growth in an active business.
"It's very active in our business sector at the moment," chairman and chief executive Rod Aldridge told Reuters in a telephone interview.
"Outsourcing is certainly something which has caught the imagination of people who are letting contracts because it does enable them to reduce costs and to improve services."

Aldridge said the group was waiting to hear on "quite a number of bids at the moment" and with cash balances standing at 13.3 million stg at the halfway stage, it was well placed should it win any of these contracts.
"Substantial growth can be funded from within the cash resources that we have," he added.
The group announced a further three contract extensions for its business services division in the first half of the financial year worth about 10 million stg.

These comprise its IT contract with Welwyn & Hatfield District Council, the revenue collection contract with the Royal Borough of Kensington & Chelsea and its IT contract with the National Health Service Pensions Agency.
Capita also said its property services division secured a contract worth some three million stg to provide professional support services to the Employment Service.
Across the group as a whole, 50 million stg of contracts and contract extensions were awarded in the first half.

Earlier, the group reported a 54 percent jump in pre-tax profits to 7.1 million stg for the six months to June 30 and 58 percent increase in turnover to 79.1 million. It proposes a 32 percent rise in the interim dividend to 0.7p a share.
Forecasts for the year point to pre-tax profits of about 17 million stg on turnover of around 170 million.

"For the full year the numbers that are out for us we are comfortable and confident about because what we've got is the raw material in the contracts we already have to make those numbers," said Aldridge.
As for the dividend he said the group usually pays one-third at the interim and two-thirds at the full year. "We'd expect to continue with that."
At 0800 GMT its share price was down 4-1/2p at 244-1/2.
